answers_to_the_commands_questions.quoted_lists_only_or_also_unquoted_enume: QUOTED AND PARENTHESISED ONLY, and the exhibit that decides it is criterion 6 itself — the single committed instance, which quotes its four tokens inside parentheses. Convention 21: exhibits precede leniency, and an unquoted enumeration after 'avoids' would widen the strongest test in the check on speculation. A criterion with a prohibition marker and no extractable quoted list falls back to presence, which fails closed. Criterion 4 of the same plan is the exhibit for that fallback: 'No claim about a named competitor appears without a clear flag' reads as a prohibition, names no forbidden vocabulary because it prohibits a SITUATION, scored 64% and passed on overlap correctly. The quote requirement also does a second job: criterion 6 carries TWO parentheses, and the structure-conventions one — '(sentence case headings, no H4+, numbers as words below 10, dates as 12 March 2026)' — is a presence-shaped aside. Reading it as forbidden would have banned the draft from being correct.

results.implementation: Three shapes, classified deterministically and free. PROHIBITION first because it is the strictly stronger test: its forbidden tokens become the test, pass iff none appear, word-boundary and case-insensitive, multi-word tokens matched as phrases with whitespace collapsed. FORM second: a structural verb plus at least two distinct field-vocabulary words, which abstains. PRESENCE is everything else, byte-identical — same _terms, same _STOPWORDS, same 0.5 threshold.
results.the_form_rule_and_why_it_is_narrow: Form is exhibited exactly once, by criterion 3, so the rule is built to catch that and refuse to guess further. Two distinct field words are demanded so a single incidental noun cannot make a measurable criterion unmeasurable — criterion 1 of the same plan uses 'includes' and stays presence, criterion 2 uses 'contains' and stays presence. This is also where B17-R1 beats the superseded Blueprint 018, which located a criterion's component by heading heuristics; that was an unexhibited guess about document structure.
results.replay_against_the_committed_demonstrati: PASSES, and the replay is verifiably against the right draft. On the final iteration's summary the four presence criteria score 0.80, 0.63, 0.64, 0.78 — IDENTICAL to the four the run recorded. Criterion 6 becomes 1.0 (no banned word present) where it scored 0.40; criterion 3 abstains where it scored 0.37. coverage.passed goes False -> True on the iteration where the run died.
results.THE_PREDICTION_IS_REFUTED_BEFORE_ANY_SPE: Section 29.3 registered the advisor's prediction that 'coverage.passed == true at ITERATION 1'. Replaying all seven committed iterations: False, False, False, False, False, False, TRUE. coverage.passed is true on exactly ONE iteration, the last. At iteration 1 it is False — the draft genuinely had not addressed criteria 1, 2 and 4, scoring 0.53, 0.37 and 0.29, and the presence check was right about that. So the ruling does NOT produce a terminal at iteration 1, and anyone reading ARCH-20260922-010's result against that wording would score a success as a failure. What the evidence supports is narrower and still decisive: coverage stops being the thing that could never be satisfied. Reported now, from free evidence, so -010's pre-registration can state a prediction that can actually be scored. This is convention 7 applied to the advisor's own prediction, and it cost nothing.
results.drift_protection_proved_not_assumed: tests/test_coverage_shapes.py::TestPresenceIsUnchanged::test_topic_mentioning_waffle_still_fails is the falsification test. The 0-33% 'names every topic while committing to nothing' exhibit still fails, still reports addressed == 0, and asserts additionally that NOTHING abstained and every shape resolved to presence — so a future widening of the classifier cannot pass this test by abstaining its way past the drift the check exists to catch.

deviations.what: One existing test failed and the CODE was changed, not the test — but not the way the test asked (convention 17).
deviations.why: tests/test_graph.py asserted the phrase 'not visibly addressed' in the detail. 'Visibly' is the word that keeps the presence test honest: it can only say the implementation never mentions what a criterion is about. It is WRONG for a prohibition, where the failure is a banned token that is plainly visible. So the verb now follows the shapes that actually failed — 'not visibly addressed by' when every failure is presence, 'not met by' when a prohibition failed. The test passes unmodified.
deviations.impact: One word of the detail string is now conditional. The test that pinned it still pins it for its own case.

deviations.what: The first replay used verdicts.implement.summary and produced WRONG scores, which I nearly reported.
deviations.why: The section 27.3 overwrite: verdicts.coverage and verdicts.implement hold verdicts from DIFFERENT iterations. Replaying the last implement summary against the last coverage verdict compares two different moments and gave 0.6/0.37/0.29/0.78 against the recorded 0.8/0.63/0.64/0.78. The iterations list carries matched pairs and is what the tests read. The exact four-way score match is the evidence that the right pair is now being compared.
deviations.impact: None to the result. Recorded because section 27.3 was written as an incidental and has now cost real time twice — it is a live trap for anyone replaying a trace, not a footnote.

deviations.what: The diff is 188 lines in autornd/graph/checks.py plus a 205-line new test file, against a stated ceiling of 300.
deviations.why: The ceiling is met by the code. Convention 22 demands an instrument's test simulate its condition end to end, and there are three shapes plus a falsification case plus a trace replay. Cutting tests to make a line budget would be the wrong trade in this repo.

questions_for_advisor: URGENT FOR -010: section 29.3's prediction says 'coverage.passed == true at iteration 1' and the free replay says False at iteration 1 and True only at iteration 7. The pre-registration for -010 must not restate the iteration-1 wording. I propose it predicts instead: (a) coverage no longer fails on a prohibition- or form-shaped criterion at any iteration, and (b) the run reaches a terminal within its ceiling. Both are scorable; the original is already refuted.

All-abstained semantics are mine by default and should not be. If every criterion is form-shaped, B17-R1's 'an abstention never fails the check' makes the check PASS with nothing measured. I implemented that, with the detail reading 'nothing measurable: all N success criteria abstained on shape' and an all_abstained flag, so it cannot be mistaken for a clean bill. But a plan whose entire contract the instrument cannot read arguably should not hand the loop a green judge at all, and that is a ruling about what the harness concludes.

The dedicated shape aggregate beside normalised_by_kind needs autornd/evals/runner.py and, for per-iteration shapes, a fix to the section 27.3 outputs overwrite. Neither is in this command's scope. Should they ride -009, which is already in the executor's engine files, or take their own command?
